analysis:
Both units are BASE-side text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 369-808). The PR diff for this file is documentation only: a new v0.10.10 candidate section is added at head lines 11-39, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The supplied base text holds older, already-published release notes, so I found no security-relevant change to examine in the supplied lines. The unit text contains no executable code or configuration.

The new v0.10.10 notes describe waitlist approval gating for `darkbloom sandbox setup` and new cluster pairing, fetched from the coordinator. They state a fail-closed refusal path (exit 1 on waitlisted, not approved, not logged in, or coordinator unreachable). They also say that existing sandbox installs and existing pairs stay unaffected, and that `cluster local` needs no approval and works offline.

If the implementation follows this description, these gates would relate to TB-013 and T-061 (sandbox installer) and to the pairing flow. The implementing code is not in the supplied evidence. The changelog line that `--yes` adds the account to the sandbox waitlist without asking is a UX statement and not a vulnerability. The changelog says that if the coordinator does not offer waitlists yet, both new setups go on as in 0.10.9. That reads as a fail-open fallback for the gate, but the head text is truncated and the code is not supplied, so no finding is justified.

A next pass should check the actual waitlist implementation. It should confirm that the approval check is server-authoritative and cannot be bypassed by a local flag. It should also confirm that the fail-open behavior applies only to a coordinator that does not offer waitlists, not to network errors. Finally, it should confirm that the offline `cluster local` path cannot be used to serve through Darkbloom. No threat-model update is needed from changelog text alone.
